description: All examination records with no ID are lumped into one group that is treated like a patient.

b.request: For each ID in Examination, including one group for all NULL-ID rows, count records and divide by total Examination rows to get its share. Among groups with share above the mean share across groups, return one unrounded row with the average count, the average share, and the average of (share − mean share)
b.sql: WITH total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM Examination), groups AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT n FROM total) AS share FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), stats AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS mean_share FROM groups), above AS (SELECT g.cnt, g.share, g.share - s.mean_share AS diff FROM groups g, stats s WHERE g.share > s.mean_share) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(diff) AS avg_share_minus_mean FROM above;

a.request: Group the Examination records by `ID` and count the records in each group. All records whose `ID` is missing are counted together as one more group, which is included in the total, in the average share, and in the filtering. Divide each group's count by the total of all group counts to get its share, find the plain average of the shares, and keep the groups whose share is above it. Return one unrounded row with: the kept groups' average record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share.
a.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), tot AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM grp), shares AS (SELECT grp.ID, grp.cnt, grp.cnt * 1.0 / tot.total AS share FROM grp, tot), avg_s AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT shares.cnt, shares.share FROM shares, avg_s WHERE shares.share > avg_s.avg_share) SELECT AVG(kept.cnt) AS avg_record_count, AVG(kept.share) AS avg_share, AVG(kept.share - avg_s.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM kept, avg_s;

c.request: Count the Examination records for each `ID` and express each count as a share of the total. For the IDs whose share is above the average share, what are their average record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their share beats the average share? Give one unrounded row. All examination records with no ID are lumped into one group that is treated like a patient.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), shares AS (SELECT ID, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM counts) AS share FROM counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_s FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_record_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_s) AS avg_share_excess FROM shares s, avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_s;

d.request: Among the examination records, treat any record with no ID as its own patient group, so the count, share, and averages are computed with that group included. For the IDs whose share is above the average share, what are their average record count, average share, and average amount by which their share exceeds the average share, with records lacking an ID counted as one group, returned as one unrounded row?
d.sql: WITH keyed AS (SELECT CASE WHEN ID IS NULL THEN 'noid_' || rowid ELSE CAST(ID AS TEXT) END AS gkey FROM Examination), grp AS (SELECT gkey, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM keyed GROUP BY gkey), tot AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM grp), shares AS (SELECT gkey, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT total FROM tot) AS share FROM grp), avgs AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_record_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM shares s, avgs a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
